messages:
Kenji Nakamura: Dropping early wireframes for the onboarding checklist entry point + step drawer. Figma: https://figma.com/file/ri-onboarding-checklist-wip (page “Entry points”) :eyes:

Tessa Morgan: ty. quick skim: overall direction feels good. main q: where are we landing the entry point? top-level Console home vs inside Hosted API → Overview?

Marissa Cole: +1. from product side, want it visible for net-new tenants but not screaming at established accounts.

Kenji Nakamura: current concept is a “Get to production” card on Console Home (top of main column) + secondary entry in left nav under “Hosted API”.

Jean-Paul Laurent: wording nit: “Get to production” might be a little intense for folks who just want to test one call. can we make it feel like “Setup checklist” / “Launch checklist”?

Tessa Morgan: agree. also “production” is charged. we should reserve “First production launch” phrasing for later steps, not the entry point.

Wei Chen: from docs side, we’re calling the canonical doc “First production launch checklist”. but in-product could be “Onboarding checklist” and the doc title can stay longer.

Elliot Price: yeah, IA doc uses “Onboarding checklist” as the umbrella. step groupings: “Start”, “Harden”, “Launch”. maybe entry point is “Onboarding checklist”.

Kenji Nakamura: makes sense. in the wireframe, the card title is currently 28 chars available (1 line), 2 lines if we allow wrap but then it fights with metrics widgets.

Tessa Morgan: we need hard constraints. can we confirm max chars for card title + step name + step description? otherwise we’re guessing.

Dylan Brooks: jumping in w/ some UI realities from Console: left rail truncates at ~24–26 chars depending on viewport. card titles can wrap but we try to avoid >2 lines. step list in drawer: we can do 1 line + ellipsis, tooltip on hover.

Kenji Nakamura: ok. propose:
- Entry card title: max 32 chars (wrap allowed, but target 1 line)
- Step title: max 36 chars (1 line)
- Step helper text (optional): max 90 chars (2 lines)
Thoughts?

Tessa Morgan: step title 36 is tight but good. helper text 90 sounds right. I’d like “helper text” to be optional and only when it reduces support tickets.

Jean-Paul Laurent: +1. if helper text exists, it should answer “why do I care” not restate the title.

Marissa Cole: re entry point placement: i’m concerned Home is getting busy. what about a dismissible banner the first time you land on Hosted API Overview?

Kenji Nakamura: I mocked a banner variant too (page “Entry points” frame 6). banner has:
“Finish setup in ~10 min” + CTA “View checklist”
But banner copy length is *very* constrained.

Tessa Morgan: banner is okay if it’s tasteful + can be dismissed. but we also need a persistent place to find it later.

Dylan Brooks: persistent can be left nav “Onboarding checklist” under Hosted API section. we can feature-flag visibility based on cohort.

George Mbatha: from research: new users often don’t know where to go after creating an API key. Home is ambiguous. Hosted API Overview is where they end up. so banner on Hosted API Overview might actually be more “in the flow”.

Wei Chen: + deep link: banner CTA should land them in the checklist drawer *with step 1 expanded* (API key + env var) so they don’t bounce.

Kenji Nakamura: yep, current click behavior: opens right drawer, focuses first incomplete step, auto-scroll to it.

Tessa Morgan: copy: “Finish setup in ~10 min” — we should be careful. if it’s 10 min for python but 30 min for enterprise network policies, it’ll feel wrong.

Marissa Cole: for MVP cohorts this is Hosted API self-serve. so 10 min is plausible for “first success”, but not for “first production launch”. maybe: “Make your first request in minutes”?

Jean-Paul Laurent: I like “Make your first request in minutes”. feels less promise-y.

Elliot Price: and aligns with TTFS language. could be “Make your first successful request” but that’s long.

Kenji Nakamura: banner variant:
Title: “Make your first request in minutes” (31 chars)
Body: “Follow the checklist to avoid common setup issues.” (53)
CTA: “Open checklist”
Dismiss “x”

Tessa Morgan: good. CTA “Open checklist” is fine. alternatively “View checklist” (more standard).

Dylan Brooks: “Open checklist” maps better to opening a drawer vs navigating. but we can make it navigate to a dedicated page later. either is fine.

Marissa Cole: we should decide if checklist is a page or drawer long term. MVP drawer is ok, but we can’t paint ourselves into a corner with copy.

Kenji Nakamura: agreed. I’ll stick with “View checklist” to keep it neutral.

Tessa Morgan: step naming: please avoid gerunds where possible. “Create API key” not “Creating an API key”. short, imperative.

Jean-Paul Laurent: also we should avoid jargon like “pin model version” without “(recommended)”. users don’t know why.

Wei Chen: can we add a “Recommended” badge on some steps rather than stuffing copy? (like “Model pinning” step marked recommended)

Dylan Brooks: doable. badge adds visual noise though. maybe only in step detail view, not list.

Kenji Nakamura: wireframe has “Required” and “Recommended” tags in the step detail header, not in list. list stays clean.

Tessa Morgan: that’s the right compromise.

George Mbatha: another note: people interpret checklists as “blocking”. we should signal that it’s guidance. microcopy like “You can come back anytime.” somewhere.

Kenji Nakamura: where would you put that? banner body? or inside drawer header?

Tessa Morgan: drawer header. something like “Track setup steps. Come back anytime.” keep it short.

Marissa Cole: + ensure dismissal doesn’t remove the nav entry. dismissal should only hide the banner.

Dylan Brooks: yup, banner dismissal is per-user per-tenant stored in prefs; nav stays.

Kenji Nakamura: ok action items:
1) Update entry point copy to “Make your first request in minutes” + “View checklist”
2) Confirm char limits w/ Console components (I’ll sync w/ Dylan)
3) Add drawer header microcopy “Come back anytime”
4) Ensure tags only show in step detail
Will post updated frames EOD.

Tessa Morgan: :thumbsup: ping me on updated frames. also please test truncated titles with worst-case step names (quotas/budgets ones get long).

Wei Chen: I’ll send you a list of “long” step titles from the checklist template so we can sanity check truncation.

Kenji Nakamura: perfect, ty.
